localHook: Los Angeles in 2025 became something different. The January Eaton fire in Altadena and the Palisades fire on the Westside together produced the most destructive wildfire event in the city’s recorded history—and the damage did not stop at the fire perimeter. Smoke, soot, and airborne ash moved through neighborhoods miles from the active burn, contaminating HVAC systems, embedding in porous materials, and depositing toxic particulate on surfaces in homes that never saw a flame. That layer of wildfire damage sits on top of Los Angeles’s existing restoration profile: a century-old plumbing network in Craftsman bungalows and Spanish-revival apartment courts, high-density water intrusion in mid-century apartment buildings, and storm-drain systems that overflow when the city gets a real rain event. Gallagher Restoration Co. has been working Los Angeles from Canyon Lake via SR-60 for over 15 years. The wildfire calls since January 2025 have added a new dimension to that history.

neighborhoods.heading: From downtown to the Westside—Los Angeles covered

items.name: Downtown & Koreatown
items.body: Dense urban construction with a mix of century-old commercial buildings, 1920s–40s residential, and modern high-rise. Aging plumbing systems and shared drainage infrastructure create water-intrusion calls that require precise scope control to contain in multi-unit environments.

items.name: Hollywood & Silver Lake
items.body: Classic LA bungalow and apartment-court stock from the 1920s through 1940s. Original plumbing, tight lot configurations, and shared walls complicate water damage containment. Silver Lake also sits close enough to the January 2025 Altadena fire corridor that smoke infiltration was documented here.

items.name: West LA & Mid-City
items.body: Mid-century residential and newer construction with a mix of apartment buildings and single-family homes. High-density water intrusion—roof leaks, appliance failures, and shared-wall pipe bursts—is the most common call. The Palisades fire smoke zone extended east through West LA in January 2025.

items.name: Altadena-adjacent & hillside neighborhoods
items.body: The January 2025 Eaton fire produced direct structural losses in Altadena and smoke infiltration across a wide swath of northeast LA neighborhoods. Gallagher’s wildfire-specific services—including Altadena and Palisades zone response—address both direct fire damage and the broader contamination footprint.

commonDamage.heading: What damages Los Angeles homes most

items.title: Wildfire smoke, soot, and post-fire contamination
items.body: The January 2025 Eaton and Palisades fires left a contamination footprint that extends well beyond burned structures. Soot and toxic ash settled on surfaces, entered HVAC systems, and embedded in porous materials across a wide swath of the city. Gallagher’s dedicated wildfire restoration services—including specific response for the Altadena and Palisades zones—address the full contamination scope.

items.title: Century-old plumbing systems
items.body: Los Angeles’s oldest residential neighborhoods carry original or early-replaced plumbing in buildings from the 1900s through 1930s. Galvanized supply lines, cast-iron stacks, and lead-joint fittings fail without warning inside plaster walls and under century-old flooring. Full cavity assessment is required, not surface repair.

items.title: High-density apartment water intrusion
items.body: Mid-century apartment courts and high-density residential buildings in Koreatown, Mid-City, and Hollywood present containment challenges unique to multi-unit construction. A pipe failure on the fourth floor affects units below it before anyone calls. Rapid assessment, containment, and coordinated access are essential.

items.title: Storm-drain overflow downtown
items.body: Los Angeles’s storm-drain infrastructure was designed for typical Southern California rainfall—not the concentrated rain events that El Niño cycles produce. Downtown and low-lying areas absorb drainage backup into lower-level commercial and residential spaces. Gallagher responds during active rain events.

howWeWork.heading: What a Los Angeles call looks like
howWeWork.body: Call (951) 541-0034 at any hour—a real person answers. Gallagher dispatches from Canyon Lake; the drive to central Los Angeles is roughly 90 minutes via SR-60 West and I-10 West. On arrival, the crew performs a full-scope assessment with professional-grade moisture meters and thermal imaging. In multi-unit buildings, scope assessment includes adjacent units when necessary. In wildfire-affected homes, the assessment includes HVAC contamination, surface soot sampling locations, and porous material inventory. You get a clear picture of findings before equipment is placed. Documentation starts immediately: photos, moisture logs, written scope. That record is what insurance adjusters need. Gallagher coordinates directly with major insurance carriers on your behalf—handling adjuster communication so you are not managing two conversations while your home or building is compromised. The same crew carries the job from first call to final reconstruction.

whyChoose.heading: Why Los Angeles homeowners call Gallagher
whyChoose.body: Los Angeles’s restoration needs in 2025 and 2026 are not what they were in 2024. The January wildfire events created a scale of contamination that requires contractors with both wildfire-specific protocols and broad restoration capability—from century-old bungalow plumbing failures to high-rise water intrusion to Altadena post-fire cleanup. Gallagher is a family-owned operation with 15 years of experience across Southern California. IICRC-trained crews apply consistent protocols across all damage categories. Aaron’s team carries full accountability from first call to final walkthrough—no national franchise routing, no mid-project handoffs. Assessment is always free. Direct insurance carrier coordination is standard. For January 2025 wildfire losses specifically, Gallagher offers dedicated wildfire restoration services for both the Altadena and Palisades fire zones. The drive from Canyon Lake is roughly 90 minutes. The work standard does not change because the address is Los Angeles.

pricing.heading: Honest numbers on restoration cost in Los Angeles
pricing.body: Assessment is free. Most residential restoration jobs in Los Angeles fall between $2,000 and $25,000 depending on damage category, affected materials, and discovery timing. Multi-unit water intrusion jobs trend higher due to containment complexity and coordinated access requirements. Post-wildfire decontamination scopes vary widely based on proximity to the burn perimeter, HVAC exposure, and the extent of soot infiltration into porous materials. Gallagher works directly with major insurance carriers—including those handling the large volume of wildfire claims from January 2025—and prepares full adjuster documentation on every job.

faqs.q: How long does it take Gallagher to reach Los Angeles?
faqs.a: From Canyon Lake HQ, the typical drive to central Los Angeles is roughly 90 minutes via SR-60 West and I-10 West. Times vary by specific neighborhood. A real person answers every call at any hour and dispatches without delay.

faqs.q: Do you handle post-wildfire cleanup from the January 2025 Eaton and Palisades fires?
faqs.a: Yes. Gallagher has dedicated wildfire restoration services for both the Altadena and Palisades fire zones. Scope includes direct fire and smoke damage, soot and ash contamination on surfaces and in HVAC systems, and porous material remediation in homes outside the active burn perimeter.

faqs.q: Can you work in multi-unit apartment buildings in Los Angeles?
faqs.a: Yes. Multi-unit water intrusion requires containment protocols and coordinated access that differ from single-family work. Gallagher’s IICRC-trained crews assess the full affected scope including adjacent units when a pipe failure affects multiple floors.

faqs.q: Do you handle century-old plumbing failures in historic LA homes?
faqs.a: Yes. Galvanized and early-copper supply lines in Craftsman bungalows, Spanish-revival apartments, and other pre-war construction are a known failure pattern. We assess the full cavity and document everything before any drying or reconstruction begins.

faqs.q: What does restoration cost in Los Angeles?
faqs.a: Assessment is always free. Most residential jobs fall between $2,000 and $25,000. Multi-unit and wildfire-contamination scopes can run higher. Gallagher coordinates with major insurance carriers and handles all adjuster documentation on your behalf.
